newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL'S MIJATOVIC HOPES FOR A GOAL -- AND A BOOKING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL'S MIJATOVIC HOPES FOR A GOAL -- AND A BOOKING.

text.p: Real Madrid striker Predrag Mijatovic does not just hope to score in this Sunday's game against Zaragoza, he also hopes to be booked for taking his shirt off during the goal celebrations.

Mijatovic, along with Real's Christian Panucci and Clarence Seedorf, says he will look for his fifth yellow card of the season in the game so as to serve suspension while on international duty in a World Cup qualifier the following week.
The Montenegrin forward, who turns out for Yugoslavia, is determined to ensure that any suspension coincides with his enforced absence from Real's game at Tenerife.

"Since we won't be in Tenerife...we will look for the fifth yellow card. It's easy to get it...but it will definitely not be talking with the referee, in case he shows you the red card," said Mijatovic.
"For example, I could take my shirt off celebrating a goal."
Yugoslavia face the Czech Republic in a European group six qualifier in Prague on April 2.
Seedorf and Panucci, who will be with the Dutch and Italian sides respectively, are less likely to score but say they may also look for a booking.
They could then serve their Spanish suspensions while away with the Netherlands, who face San Marino on March 29, and Italy, who host Moldova on the same day.
Real president Lorenzo Sanz says he will not punish the players.
"Why should we be stupid about it? Of course I would understand it and I won't recriminate them for it," said Sanz.
With 39 points left in contention, Sanz's team are a comfortable nine points ahead of Barcelona and Betis.
Real have an unerring ability to absorb pressure before unleashing Mijatovic and fellow strikers Davor Suker and Raul Gonzalez.
Last Monday's game at Real Sociedad was a typical example of the discipline former AC Milan coach Fabio Capello has instilled in the team.
The Madrid side were against the ropes for much of the first half before a moment of vision from Mijatovic set up Raul, who had no problems opening the scoring.
Raul put through Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos to make it 2-0 and despite once again falling victim to a headed goal Mijatovic's side were able to hang on for the 2-1 victory.
"We're very close, we need the last few steps but until we are mathematically champions we must keep working at full capacity," said Mijatovic.
This weekend Real will come up against a revitalised Zaragoza side that includes former Real overlapping defender Miguel Soler.

Soler went for more than six months without a club after failing to see his contract with Real renewed but he was snapped up by Zaragoza over the New Year after coming close to joining the Spanish exodus to the Mexican league.
